name: pe-get-gmt
why: PEGetGMTTimeOfDay -> shim_mcu_get_gmt (Thumb: ldr r3,[pc]; bx r3): Unix time from the 3DS MCU RTC (ARM9 mailbox, docs/mcu.md); without an RTC the shim runs the original body (gIOPlatform->getGMTTimeOfDay(), vtable +0x390)

name: iortc-wait-mcu
why: IOKitInitializeTime (0x801a8004): literal of its waitForService(resourceMatching("IORTC"), {2 s}) call -> shim_mcu_wait_rtc: no wait when the MCU RTC is known (the calendar no longer depends on AppleARMPE), else the original call with iortc-wait-2s' 2 s timeout

name: pe-set-gmt
why: PESetGMTTimeOfDay -> shim_mcu_set_gmt: AppleARMPE::setGMTTimeOfDay (0x802e7834) waits 30 s for an IORTC that never appears; the shim keeps iOS' time as an offset to the RTC instead (the 3DS RTC is not written)

name: pe-halt-mcu
why: PEHaltRestart: gIOPlatform->haltRestart(type) (ldr r2,[r0]; movs r3,#0xe2; lsls; adds r1,r5,#0; ldr r3,[r2,r3]) -> adds r1,r5,#0; ldr r3,[pc,#0]; b +2; .word shim_mcu_halt_restart; the blx r3 at 0x801c9900 stays. Halt/restart power the console off through the MCU (ARM9), other types go to the platform as before

name: commpage-gtod-off
why: commpage_set_timestamp (0x8006ade0): beq -> b, the gettimeofday timestamp is never published. Userland __commpage_gettimeofday (dyld cache 0x32d4b748) adds (now - base) / usec_divisor via a reciprocal the kernel computes here; our timebase is 1047311 Hz, so usec_divisor = 1 and the reciprocal degenerates (M = 0, add = 1, shift = 0 -> a shift by -1): elapsed time always reads 0 and gettimeofday() stays frozen at the last syscall refresh for up to 1 s (gltest '0 ms', '1063 ms vs mach 412 ms', docs/mcu.md section 8). With the base left at 0 userland always takes the gettimeofday syscall, which is exact
